notes: Batch 01 was intentionally stopped after the sign-flip control because the baseline was negative and the sign-flip control still failed the practical floor on the official alpha checks.
The remaining ts-rank variants were not launched because the first decisive control already showed a low-ceiling, cosmetic-variation pattern.
All metrics below come from the official logged-in WorldQuant BRAIN Simulate page and alpha API in this session.

alphas.name: scl12_sentiment_fast_d1
notes: IS is clearly negative and fails LOW_SHARPE, LOW_FITNESS, HIGH_TURNOVER, CONCENTRATED_WEIGHT, and LOW_SUB_UNIVERSE_SHARPE.
The holdout/test slice stays noisy and does not suggest a stable rescue path.
This baseline is not worth polishing further inside the same source family.

alphas.name: neg_scl12_sentiment_fast_d1
notes: The sign flip rescues the IS sign but still misses the practical floor: LOW_SHARPE fail, LOW_FITNESS fail, HIGH_TURNOVER fail, and CONCENTRATED_WEIGHT fail.
The holdout/test slice flips negative, so this is not a stable sign-orientation fix.
This was enough evidence to freeze the family without launching the remaining lookback variants.

decision.reason: Baseline is negative; sign-flip control is still weak on IS and reverses to negative on test. The family ceiling is low and the remaining lookback variants would be cosmetic.
